messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: file uploading
parts:
Try this (this is just the output of fileInput("fileChoice", "Choose File") ). The idea is that file inputs return a dataframe with each row corresponding to a file uploaded. You have to use the datapath column to get its path and read it.

<label>Choose File</label>
<input id="fileChoice" type="file"/>
<div id="fileChoice_progress" class="progress progress-striped active shiny-file-input-progress">
  <div class="bar"></div>
  <label></label>
</div>

# server.R
output$tab <- renderTable({
  # infile is a data frame with four columns
  # do ? fileInput for details
  inFile <- input$fileChoice
  if (is.null(inFile))
    return(NULL)    
  read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=TRUE, sep=input$sep)
})

messages.subject: Re: file uploading
parts:
Try these instead:

fileSeparator <- reactive({
switch(input$fileSeparator,
                   comma=',',
                   semicolonne=';',

tab='\t',
                   exp = rexp
                   )
  })
output$tab <- renderTable({

inFile <- input$fileChoice
          if (is.null(inFile))
          return(NULL)

read.csv(inFile$datapath, input$header, sep=fileSeparator(), dec='.', row.names=NULL)
   })

In answer to your other question: checkboxes in particular can work in two different ways. 1) The checkbox represents a boolean value (TRUE/FALSE) and no other checkbox has anything to do with it. 2) The checkbox is part of a group of checkboxes that all share the same name; the value of input$name is a character vector containing all the values, or a zero-length vector if none are checked. These two cases are completely different; we use id="..." vs. name="..." to distinguish between the two.

If you use ui.R then you don't have to worry about how we implement this difference; just use checkboxInput for the first case, and checkboxGroupInput for the second. In general, ui.R is going to be easier than index.html, and doesn't suffer any loss of control since ui.R can express arbitrary HTML constructions using R code. See ?tags.

In answer to your other question: checkboxes in particular can work in two different ways. 1) The checkbox represents a boolean value (TRUE/FALSE) and no other checkbox has anything to do with it. 2) The checkbox is part of a group of checkboxes that all share the same name; the value of input$name is a character vector containing all the values, or a zero-length vector if none are checked. These two cases are completely different; we use id="..." vs. name="..." to distinguish between the two.

If you use ui.R then you don't have to worry about how we implement this difference; just use checkboxInput for the first case, and checkboxGroupInput for the second. In general, ui.R is going to be easier than index.html, and doesn't suffer any loss of control since ui.R can express arbitrary HTML constructions using R code. See ?tags.
